questions.q: The correct order of 2^{nd} ionization energy for the elements carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and fluorine is
questions.solution:
The second ionisation energy means the energy required to remove the electron from the corresponding monovalent cation of the respective atom. For $\text{I}{\text{E}_{2},$ electronic. Configuration of ${\textC^{+}, {\textN^{+}, {\textO^{+}$ and ${\textF^{+}$ -ions which are as follows.

${\textC^{+} = 2{\texts^{2}, 2{\textp^{1}$

${\textN^{+} = 2{\texts^{2}, 2{\textp^{2}$

${\textO^{+} = 2{\texts^{2}, 2{\textp^{3}$

${\textF^{+} = 2{\texts^{2}, 2{\textp^{4}$

$∵ {\textO^{+}$ is half - filed configuration, obviously it is most stable and greater ionization energy than ${\textF^{+}$ as well as

${\textN^{+}$. The ionisation energy of an element depends upon its size as. $\text{I}\text{E} ∝ \dfrac{1}{\text{Size of atom} / \text{ion}}$ smaller the atom/ion,

larger mill be IE.

Hence, correct order will be, $\text{O} > \text{F} > \text{N} > \text{C}$
